findings.claim: Delete calls recordStorageDuration with the object `name` as the `kind` label value. Each deleted object name creates a new histogram series, so label cardinality is unbounded.
findings.evidence: metrics.go declares the labels [is_error, mode, kind, method]. Every other call passes options.Kind. instrumentation.md requires a pre-defined set of label values. The same slip is at dualwriter_mode1.go:155. All seats reasoned this from source; none ran it.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test to write before fixing: call dw.Delete(ctx, "foo", ...) in Mode3, then assert with testutil.CollectAndCount that the storage-duration histogram gains no kind="foo" series. It fails on the pinned code. Fix: pass options.Kind.

verifier.reason: pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:106 passes `name` (the object name) to recordStorageDuration, which uses it as the `kind` label value (metrics.go:23, 61), while the error path at line 103 and every other call pass options.Kind. Each successful delete of a different object therefore adds a new histogram series.

findings.claim: Create's storage-error path records the failure with recordLegacyDuration (using startStorage) when it should use recordStorageDuration.
findings.evidence: Seen in the diff hunk by all four seats. It is a copy-paste drift from the duplicated timing calls. It corrupts the legacy and storage duration metrics that gate the mode-3 rollout. Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test: fresh registry with NewDualWriter(Mode3, ...) and a storage Create mock that returns an error. Then assert that CollectAndCount on the legacy-duration histogram is 0 (it is 1 on the pinned code) and that the storage histogram has is_error="true".

verifier.reason: In pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:45, the error branch after d.Storage.Create calls d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ..., startStorage). The success path at :48 calls recordStorageDuration, so storage failures are being counted as legacy failures.

findings.claim: Update's storage-error path records the failure with recordLegacyDuration when it should use recordStorageDuration.
findings.evidence: Same drift as :45, seen in the diff hunk by all four seats. Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test: the Update analogue of the :45 test. Make the storage Update mock fail, then assert the legacy histogram stays empty. It fails on the pinned code.

verifier.reason: At pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:126-129 the error comes from d.Storage.Update, yet the failure is recorded with d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...). The success path at :132 and the other storage-error paths (Delete :103, DeleteCollection :156) use recordStorageDuration, so this is mislabeled.

findings.claim: The DeleteCollection legacy goroutine records the legacy call's duration with recordStorageDuration when it should use recordLegacyDuration.
findings.evidence: Seen in the diff hunk by all four seats. Reasoned, not run.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test: run DeleteCollection with mocks and wait for the goroutine. Then assert the legacy-duration histogram has a sample and the storage histogram has exactly one. It fails on the pinned code.

verifier.reason: At pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:165-166 the goroutine calls d.Legacy.DeleteCollection, then records the time with d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy). The matching legacy goroutines in Update (line 140) and Delete call recordLegacyDuration, so legacy time here ends up in the storage metric.

findings.claim: Delete calls klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log) when it should pass `log`, so the name, kind and method fields never reach downstream loggers.
findings.evidence: Seen in the diff by all four seats. Every other method attaches `log`. The same bug is in mode 1.
findings.reason: Accepted Minor. The one-token fix is to pass `log`. No red test is required at Minor severity.

verifier.reason: At pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go:96-97, Delete builds `log` with name, kind and method but then calls `klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)`, so downstream Storage/Legacy calls get the base logger without those fields. Every other method in the file passes `log` (lines 39, 66, 82, 123, 150), and the same pattern exists in the untouched dualwriter_mode1.go:146.

findings.claim: The async legacy writes in Create, Update, Delete and DeleteCollection (lines ~51, 110, 135, 163) derive their context from the request ctx with context.WithTimeoutCause. When the handler returns, the request ctx is cancelled, so the legacy writes can be cancelled too. Legacy then silently drifts from unified storage, which breaks rollback.
findings.evidence: Before this patch the writes were synchronous. The playlist legacy store's SQL uses this ctx. Proposed fix: context.WithoutCancel (go 1.22.4). The same pattern exists at dualwriter_mode1.go:54. Reasoned; open-code-review could not read the k8s.io/apiserver cancellation source.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test: pass a cancellable ctx and cancel it right after Create returns. Give the legacy mock a blocking Run that then checks ctx.Err(). Assert the write saw a live ctx; it fails on the pinned code. If this cannot be made red in a unit test, keep the Important severity and defer it as unverified.

verifier.reason: In dualwriter_mode3.go:51, 110, 135 and 163, the background goroutines build their timeout context from the request ctx using context.WithTimeoutCause, then return right away. Go's net/http cancels the request ctx when ServeHTTP returns, so the legacy Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection can be cancelled partway through, and the only trace is a metric (lines 56, 113, 140, 166), not a log. I could not read the k8s.io/apiserver handler source here; this relies on Go's documented net/http behaviour.

findings.claim: Update now hands the caller's raw objInfo to Legacy.Update in a goroutine. UpdatedObject is then re-run against legacy's own old object after the request has ended. For PATCH and server-side apply this can give legacy a different object than storage, and may race on handler state.
findings.evidence: The patch removes the updateWrapper{updated: obj} hand-off. Legacy Update (pkg/registry/apis/playlist/legacy_storage.go:147) calls objInfo.UpdatedObject(ctx, legacyOld). Reasoned; nothing was run with -race.
findings.reason: Accepted. Red test: supply an UpdatedObjectInfo whose output depends on oldObj, with storage and legacy returning different old objects. Assert that the object the legacy mock receives equals the object storage returned. It fails on the pinned code. Fix: restore updateWrapper with a deep copy of the storage result.

verifier.reason: At dualwriter_mode3.go:139, the patch now passes the caller's raw objInfo to Legacy.Update inside a fire-and-forget goroutine and drops the old updateWrapper{updated: obj} hand-off, so legacy_storage.go:142-147 runs objInfo.UpdatedObject again against legacy's own Get result. For PATCH and apply, the patch gets re-applied to legacy's copy, which can differ from what storage saved, and the request's patcher state is reused after the handler has returned.

findings.claim: legacyStoreMock and storageMock share one *mock.Mock, so the mode-3 unit tests cannot verify mode 3's contract. Nothing checks that reads skip legacy or that legacy is written. Legacy expectations are dead or misleading; for example, the Create case 'unified store fails' passes only because the storage call matches the setupLegacyFn expectation. There are no AssertExpectations or AssertNotCalled calls and no wait for the goroutine.
findings.evidence: Shared mock at dualwriter_mode3_test.go:37-44 / 28-42 and the Create error case at 297-325. Mode 1 tests use AssertNotCalled; mode 3 has none. The legacy setups in the Update and Create success cases duplicate or are shadowed by the storage setups.
findings.reason: Accepted. Severity set to Important, as superpowers raised it; it is also why the main-list bugs pass CI. Red test: give legacy and storage separate mock.Mock instances. The 'unified store fails' Create case then fails on the pinned code. Add AssertNotCalled on legacy for reads and a synchronised assertion that legacy is written.

verifier.reason: Every TestMode3_* case wraps the same `m := &mock.Mock{}` in both `legacyStoreMock{m, l}` and `storageMock{m, s}` (dualwriter_mode3_test.go:51-54), so the Create case 'error when creating object in the unified store fails' (lines 37-44) only reaches its error because Storage.Create matches the setupLegacyFn expectation. The duplicate legacy Update setup (313-315) is likewise indistinguishable from the storage one, and the file has no AssertExpectations, AssertNotCalled or wait for the legacy goroutines, whereas mode 1 does use AssertNotCalled (dualwriter_mode1_test.go:147).
